Full description

Responsibilities The Global Brand & Communications PMO team keeps the whole Brand, Communications, Marketing, and CSR organization running, including systems, budgets, planning cycles, cross-functional projects, and the tentpole moments that no single team can run alone. We translate fast-moving global agendas into clear workflows, well-run campaigns, and decisions leaders can actually make. You will work directly with leaders across Communications, Marketing, CSR, Finance, Legal, HR, and Product, and get a front-row seat to how a global brand really operates, not just how it presents itself. The Global Brand & Comms Operations team creates the operational foundation that enables Global Brand & Comms to do its best work. As strategic partners, the team builds the systems, standards, and ways of working that drive clarity, consistency, speed, and operational excellence across the organization. Working across Global Communications, Global CSR, and Global Marketing, we connect teams, align cross-functional partners, and ensure work moves forward efficiently and strategically around the world. The team also serves as a liaison to key XFN partners, including Procurement, Finance, Legal and Human Resources. Though individually based in AMS, APAC, and EMEA, we operate as one global PMO team with shared ways of working. PMOs work to seamlessly integrate strategy and operations to drive consistency across the Global Brand & Comms department. You help connect dots and strengthen information sharing, so teams are able to drive stronger results for the business. This includes department-level operations as well as projects that span Global Comms, Global CSR, and Global Marketing. All PMOs on the Operations team have both global and regional accountability. The role is rooted in cross-functional project management, problem-solving and planning, and organization and management of key initiatives. PMOs play a strong role in supporting both the operational functions of the department and teams within it, while also helping to manage external campaigns. Full description

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. On the Waymo Marketing team, you will help to connect people with the magic and impact of Waymo's autonomous driving technology. Our team has the unique opportunity to not only grow Waymo's brand from the ground up, but to also build societal acceptance for autonomous driving technology for the first time in history. We build thoughtful marketing strategy, positioning, messaging and creative assets to deliver messages that matter to our audience, communicated through anything from video content, to social media interactions, to immersive physical experiences. We also shape Waymo's go-to-market initiatives, helping to transform Waymo into a thriving business with a growing user base. In this hybrid role based in Los Angeles or New York, you will report to the Global Experiential Marketing Lead. You Will: Spearhead US and select global experiential marketing strategies, driving high-impact initiatives from concept through execution. Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of sponsorships and partnerships, leading property identification, strategic alignment, commercial negotiations, and on-site brand experiences. Drive end-to-end event-based strategy defining target audience segments, determining optimal event formats and scale, and establishing clear measurement frameworks to drive business impact. Serve as the steward of Waymo’s brand vision, translating brand strategy into immersive, world-class experiences that foster public trust in autonomous technology. Lead event sponsorship deal structuring and contract negotiations partnering with cross-functional partners, legal and finance teams to maximize asset value, ensure favorable commercial terms, and protect brand interests across all agreements. Mobilize leadership and cross-functional teams behind event priorities, securing rapid approvals through clear, proactive communication to execute at speed. Manage program budgets with attention to detail, optimizing resource allocation and vendor negotiations to deliver premium activations with high cost-efficiency. You Have: 10+ years in an event specific role leading high-impact experiences in the US. Deep knowledge of the region’s experiential landscape, with a strong understanding of regional event industry trends and audiences. Extensive experience navigating the event sponsorship ecosystem, with a proven ability to evaluate value, negotiate high-stakes agreements, and oversee seamless on-site asset delivery. Exceptional project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously. A roll-up-your-sleeves mentality with the flexibility to jump into operational, creative, or logistical functions to keep projects moving forward as we scale the team. A natural ability to balance high-level strategy with hands-on tactical execution, seamlessly pivoting across shifting priorities and expanding project scopes. We Prefer: Global sponsorship experience. Experience in the autonomous vehicle, mobility, or a similarly highly regulated, pioneering technology sector. Experience thriving in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Travel Requirements: 30% - Willing to travel globally as required The expected base salary range for this full-time position across US locations is listed below. Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the role location or, if the role can be performed remote, the specific salary range for your preferred location, during the hiring process. Waymo employees are also eligible to participate in Waymo’s discretionary annual bonus program, equity incentive plan, and generous Company benefits program, subject to eligibility requirements. Salary Range $210,000—$259,000 USD

Job Information Job TitleDirector, Communications Agency Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi Department Institutional Advancement Proposed Minimum SalaryCommensurate Job LocationCorpus Christi, Texas Job TypeStaff Job Description TAMU-CC is a dynamic university designated as both a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and Minority-Serving Institution (MSI) with approximately 11,000 students from 47 states and 54 foreign nations. We employ over 1,400 full-time and 2,000 part-time Islanders (including students/GAs). The University attracts highly talented faculty and staff and offers an array of undergraduate and graduate degrees, including doctoral programs. As a member of the Texas A&M University System, TAMU-CC benefits from a range of resources, increased visibility and influence, and opportunities to collaborate in mutually beneficial ways with peers across member institutions and associated agencies. TAMU-CC’s beautiful campus is located on a 240-acre island on Corpus Christi Bay and was ranked #1 College by the Sea by Best College Reviews. Our natural setting is enhanced by its modern, attractive, and state-of-the-art classroom buildings and support facilities. Responsibilities Functional Area 1: Strategic & Institutional Communications Percent Effort: 35% Develop and execute comprehensive communications strategies that advance university priorities, including enrollment, student success, research, advancement, community engagement, and institutional reputation. Establish and maintain a cohesive institutional voice and messaging framework across communications channels. Provide strategic communications counsel to university leadership on institutional initiatives, announcements, sensitive issues, and emerging opportunities. Develop executive communications, including speeches, talking points, presentations, statements, correspondence, and other leadership messaging. Oversee institutional communications and major publications, ensuring content is accurate, compelling, audience-focused, and aligned with university priorities. Collaborate with colleges, divisions, and university leadership to identify communications opportunities and coordinate messaging across the institution. Develop an overarching strategic communication plan and toolkit to support major university initiatives, announcements, events, and milestones. Provide communications guidance and standards to campus communicators to strengthen consistency and coordination across the university. Functional Area 2: Media Relations & Reputation Management Percent Effort: 25% Serve as the university’s primary media relations contact and spokesperson, as appropriate. Develop and maintain strong relationships with local, regional, national, and industry-specific media. Lead proactive media outreach and story development highlighting faculty expertise, research, student success, institutional accomplishments, community impact, and university priorities. Oversee press releases, media advisories, statements, feature stories, media pitches, and other external communications. Coordinate media interviews, press conferences, and media opportunities involving university leadership, faculty, staff, and subject‑matter experts. Prepare university representatives for media interviews through messaging, talking points, briefing materials, and media preparation. Monitor media coverage, emerging issues, public sentiment, and reputational trends; provide analysis and recommendations to university leadership. Identify emerging reputational opportunities and risks and recommend proactive communications strategies. Functional Area 3: Crisis & Issues Communications Percent Effort: 20% Lead the university’s crisis and issues communications strategy in coordination with university leadership and appropriate campus partners. Develop, maintain, and regularly evaluate the university’s crisis communications plan, protocols, templates, and response procedures. Serve as the communications lead within the university’s Incident Command structure during emergencies and significant incidents. Develop and coordinate timely, accurate communications for internal and external audiences across email, web, social media, media relations, emergency notification systems, and other channels. Advise university leadership on communications strategy during emergencies, sensitive situations, and reputational issues. Coordinate messaging with university police, university leadership, legal counsel, the Texas A&M University System, and other appropriate partners. Monitor media, social media, and public conversation during emerging issues and crises and recommend appropriate responses. Conduct post-incident communications reviews and incorporate lessons learned into future crisis planning. Maintain appropriate after-hours availability for time‑sensitive emergencies and reputational matters. Functional Area 4: Content Strategy & Editorial Leadership Percent Effort: 10% Provide strategic direction for university news, institutional storytelling, executive communications, and other communications content. Oversee the development of written content for digital, social, video, audio, print, and other communications channels. Establish editorial priorities that support institutional goals and strengthen the university’s reputation. Serve as final editorial authority for designated university-level communications, ensuring accuracy, consistency, AP style compliance, and alignment with institutional messaging. Partner with Marketing, Creative Services, Web, Enrollment, Advancement, academic units, and other university teams to coordinate integrated storytelling and communications. Identify opportunities to elevate faculty expertise and university thought leadership in regional, national, and industry conversations. Functional Area 5: Communications Measurement & Strategy Percent Effort: 5% Establish annual communications goals, key performance indicators, and measures of success aligned with the university’s strategic priorities. Monitor and evaluate media coverage, audience engagement, digital performance, sentiment, and other relevant communications metrics. Use data and audience insights to evaluate communications effectiveness and refine strategies. Provide regular communications and reputation reports, insights, and recommendations to university leadership. Functional Area 6: Leadership & Administration Percent Effort: 5% Lead, supervise, mentor, and develop professional communications staff. Establish team priorities, workflows, performance expectations, and professional development goals. Foster a collaborative, responsive, high‑performing culture focused on quality, service, innovation, and continuous improvement. Manage assigned communications budgets and resources. Develop and maintain communications policies, procedures, editorial standards, and standard operating procedures. Serve on university committees, task forces, emergency response teams, and working groups as assigned. Represent the university at professional, community, and industry events as appropriate. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, marketing, or a closely related field. Ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in communications, public relations, media relations, journalism, or a related field, including at least three (3) years of supervisory or leadership experience. Additional education/experience may be considered as a substitute for the minimum requirements: Master’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, marketing, or a closely related field with eight (8) years of progressively responsible professional experience in communications, public relations, media relations, journalism, or a related field, including at least three (3) years of supervisory or leadership experience. Doctoral degree in communications, public relations, journalism, marketing, or a closely related field with six (6) years of progressively responsible professional experience in communications, public relations, media relations, journalism, or a related field, including at least three (3) years of supervisory or leadership experience. Exceptional written, verbal, editing, and interpersonal communication skills. Demonstrated experience developing and implementing strategic communications plans for complex organizations. Demonstrated experience working with media and developing successful media relations strategies. Experience managing sensitive, high‑profile, or crisis communications. Strong judgment and demonstrated ability to advise leaders on complex communications matters. Ability to manage multiple priorities and make sound decisions in a fast‑paced environment. Demonstrated ability to use communications data and analytics to inform strategy and evaluate effectiveness. Ability to maintain the security and integrity of critical infrastructure, which may include communications systems, computer networks and systems, cybersecurity systems, electrical grid, hazardous waste treatment system or water treatment system. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, marketing, higher education administration, or a related field. Communications or public relations experience within higher education or another large, complex organization. Experience leading crisis and issues communications. Experience providing communications counsel to executive leadership. Experience developing regional or national media relationships and successfully pitching stories. Knowledge of emerging communications trends, media monitoring, digital communications, and reputation management. Up to 83% of premium covered by the university: Employee and Spouse Employee and Children Employee and Family coverage Dental & Vision. Life Insurance, Accidental D&D, Long Term Disability, Flexible Spending Account and Day Care Spending Account. On-campus wellness opportunities. Work Life Solutions: Counseling, Work Life Assistance, Financial Resources, and Legal Resources. Tuition Benefits: Public Loan Forgiveness Book scholarships 100% tuition coverage for up to 18 credit hours per fiscal year (other rules may apply). Retirement Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS) or Optional Retirement Plan (ORP) Voluntary Tax Deferred Account/Deferred Compensation Plan. Time Off: 8+ hours of vacation paid time off every month. 8 hours of sick leave time off every month. 8 hours of paid time off for Birthday leave. 12-15 paid holidays each year. All positions are security-sensitive. Remote/Hybrid Job Overview We're looking for a Senior Specialist, Partner Marketing Campaigns & Events to help drive the execution of partner marketing campaigns, programs, and events that strengthen partner engagement and support business growth. This role is ideal for a marketer who enjoys bringing campaigns and events to life, collaborating across teams, and creating meaningful experiences for partners through field marketing activities, industry events, meaningful content, and digital campaigns. You will play a key role in executing multi-partner marketing initiatives, managing partner participation in Relativity and industry events, and supporting marketing programs from planning through execution and measurement. You will also help guide campaign performance reporting and provide recommendations to improve future programs and partner engagement. This role combines campaign execution, event marketing, communications, and program management, making it an excellent opportunity for someone interested in growing their expertise in partner marketing. Over time, this role is designed to provide increasing exposure to partner strategy and relationship management, creating a path toward a more partner-facing partner marketing role as experience, confidence, and impact expand. Job Description and Requirements What You'll Do Own the execution of partner marketing campaigns and programs, including field marketing activities, content initiatives, webinars, and digital campaigns . Manage partner participation across Relativity-sponsored events and industry conferences, including sponsorship fulfillment, partner engagement, communications, event logistics , and post-event follow-up. Responsibilities may include supporting initiatives such as RelFest , Legalweek , ILTACON, CLOC, and other strategic industry events. Serve as a key coordinator for partner marketing activities related to major events, helping ensure a positive and consistent experience for participating partners before, during, and after each event. Manage internal partner marketing communications, including team updates, deliverables, deadlines, and visibility into priority initiatives. Execute campaign-related activities including email marketing, landing page development, content creation, social media promotion, campaign setup, and coordination with Marketing Operations and other supporting teams. Coordinate partner marketing content and communications opportunities, including social media promotion, partner announcements, public relations activities, and partner-related web content updates. Track and report on campaign and program performance, providing observations, insights, and recommendations to improve future partner marketing initiatives. Create monthly and quarterly reports that provide the Partner Marketing team with visibility into campaign, program, and event performance, highlighting key results, trends, and areas for follow-up. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Events, Product Marketing, Segment Marketing, Marketing Operations, Communications, and Sales to ensure successful campaign and program execution. What We're Looking For 5-8 years of experience in B2B marketing, preferably in tech, legal, or SaaS . Experience working in a partner marketing, channel marketing, alliance marketing, or ecosystem marketing environment, even if not in a partner-facing capacity. Experience supporting conferences, trade shows, customer events, sponsorships, or other field marketing activities. Experience executing multi-channel marketing campaigns, events, or marketing programs from planning through execution and measurement. Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple programs, stakeholders, deadlines, and competing priorities simultaneously. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing marketing communications, campaign assets, or event-related content. Comfort working with marketing performance data and campaign reporting, with the ability to identify trends and suggest opportunities for improvement. Familiarity with marketing technologies such as Salesforce, marketing automation platforms, webinar platforms, or similar tools. Collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively across multiple teams and functions. Interest in continuing to grow into a more partner-facing partner marketing role over time, with increasing exposure to partner engagement, strategic planning, and relationship management. Location This position can be remote for candidates located outside the Chicago area. Candidates based in the Chicago area are expected to work from the Chicago office at least two days per week as part of Relativity's hybrid work model. There may be limited travel to support field marketing events. If hired as a remote employee, you will be expected to travel to the Chicago office for team meetings 2-4 times per year. Relativity is committed to competitive, fair, and equitable compensation practices. This position is eligible for total compensation which includes a competitive base salary, an annual performance bonus, and long-term incentives. The expected salary range for this role is between following values: $94,000 and $142,000 The final offered salary will be based on several factors, including but not limited to the candidate's depth of experience, skill set, qualifications, and internal pay equity. xklufbp Hiring at the top end of the range would not be typical, to allow for future meaningful salary growth in this position. Required Skills: Channels Marketing, Content Marketing, Digital Marketing, Event Marketing, Lead Generation, Marketing Strategies, Partner Marketing, Public Relations (PR), Relationship Management, Sales Enablement

Passion for supporting the ink and/or beauty shop industries and communities. Ability to travel to events, for meetings and to Kansas City headquarters. Why USAA? At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful. We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs. The Opportunity We are seeking a strategic, data-driven professional to lead efforts focused on understanding and optimizing the end-to-end member journey across marketing and digital experiences. This role will partner closely with teams across Marketing, Digital, Analytics, Product, Go-to-Market, and Customer Experience to evaluate funnel performance, uncover actionable insights, and identify opportunities to improve customer outcomes. The ideal candidate brings a strong marketing and business mindset, with the ability to connect data, customer behavior, and digital experiences to drive meaningful improvements across the customer journey. This individual will serve as a key cross-functional partner, influencing strategy, facilitating collaboration, and helping shape an emerging discipline focused on funnel optimization and member experience. This is not a technical development, IT, or dashboard-building role. Rather, it is a highly collaborative business role requiring strong analytical thinking, project management, communication, and influencing skills to drive progress across multiple stakeholders and initiatives. Our marketing team supports a growing national brand through digital marketing, content, SEO, paid media, email, social media, video, website strategy, sales enablement, trade shows, product campaigns, and lead generation. As our marketing organization continues to grow, we are looking for a highly organized, proactive Marketing Project Manager who can help bring structure, accountability, and visibility to our marketing initiatives. Position Overview Western States Metal Roofing is seeking an experienced Marketing Project Manager to manage the planning, coordination, execution, and delivery of marketing projects across the organization. This role will be responsible for managing the marketing team’s workflow in Monday.com, keeping projects on schedule, coordinating across internal teams and external vendors, identifying bottlenecks, managing deadlines, and ensuring projects move from idea to completion efficiently. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, comfortable managing multiple priorities, and capable of working closely with creative, digital, content, sales, product, operations, and leadership teams. This is a hands-on project management role. The Marketing Project Manager will not simply track tasks—they will actively drive projects forward, hold stakeholders accountable, surface risks early, and help the Director of Marketing maintain visibility into priorities, workload, deadlines, and results. Key Responsibilities Manage the marketing department’s project management system in Monday.com. Build, maintain, and improve project boards, workflows, dashboards, automations, dependencies, templates, and reporting. Create clear project plans with deliverables, owners, timelines, milestones, dependencies, and deadlines. Coordinate projects across marketing functions including: Content marketing SEO Paid media Email marketing HubSpot campaigns Website projects Video production Graphic design Sales materials Product launches Trade shows and events Vendor projects Lead generation campaigns Manage campaign timelines from kickoff through launch and post-campaign review. Lead project kickoff meetings and clearly define scope, responsibilities, milestones, and deadlines. Run regular marketing project-status meetings. Follow up with project owners and stakeholders to keep deliverables moving. Identify schedule risks, scope changes, resource conflicts, and bottlenecks before they impact deadlines. Escalate project risks and unresolved issues to the Director of Marketing as needed. Maintain accurate project documentation, meeting notes, action items, approvals, and decisions. Ensure creative assets, copy, approvals, tracking, landing pages, emails, forms, reporting, and sales enablement materials are completed before campaign launch. Coordinate with internal departments such as Sales, Operations, Product, IT, and Leadership. Manage communication and timelines with outside agencies, freelancers, printers, developers, photographers, videographers, and other vendors. Track vendor deliverables and ensure projects stay within agreed scope and schedule. Support marketing budget tracking and project-level cost visibility. Help manage marketing calendars, campaign calendars, editorial calendars, trade-show schedules, and product-launch schedules. Monitor team capacity and help prioritize projects based on business impact. Maintain visibility into competing priorities and help the Director of Marketing make resource-allocation decisions. Develop repeatable processes, templates, checklists, and standard operating procedures. Conduct post-project reviews to identify what worked, what did not, and how future projects can be improved. Maintain centralized documentation for marketing processes, project standards, and workflows. Ensure projects align with larger marketing and revenue objectives. Support reporting on project completion, campaign readiness, delays, workload, and operational efficiency. Help improve cross-functional communication between Marketing and Sales. Monday.com Ownership This role will serve as the primary owner of Monday.com for the marketing department. Responsibilities will include: Creating and managing project boards Building reusable project templates Maintaining status definitions and naming conventions Creating automations and notifications Managing dependencies and timelines Building dashboards for leadership visibility Tracking overdue tasks and project risks Maintaining campaign and content calendars Monitoring workload and team capacity Improving adoption and consistency across the marketing team Training team members on proper Monday.com usage Ensuring project information stays accurate and current The goal is to make Monday.com the central source of truth for marketing projects. Required Qualifications 3+ years of project management, marketing operations, campaign management, or related experience. Experience managing multiple marketing projects simultaneously. Strong hands-on experience with Monday.com or a comparable project-management platform. Strong understanding of marketing workflows and campaign execution. Experience coordinating projects across creative, digital, content, web, social, and sales teams. Excellent organizational and time-management skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage deadlines and hold team members and stakeholders accountable. Strong attention to detail. Ability to identify risks, dependencies, and potential project delays. Experience managing outside vendors or agencies. Comfortable working with multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and take ownership of projects. Comfortable communicating with both individual contributors and senior leadership. Proficiency with Microsoft Office or Google Workspace. Compensation amp; Benefits $75,000 annual salary Full-time position On-site at our Phoenix, Arizona campus Competitive employee benefits package Paid time off Company holidays Health and other employee benefits Opportunities for professional growth and increased responsibility Work Schedule This is a full-time, on-site position based at our Phoenix campus. The Marketing Project Manager will work closely with the Director of Marketing and collaborate across the organization to ensure marketing projects are properly planned, prioritized, executed, and completed. Apply If you are highly organized, enjoy managing complex projects, are comfortable holding teams accountable, and want to help build a more efficient and scalable marketing organization, we would like to hear from you. Please submit your resume and include examples of marketing projects, campaigns, or project-management systems you have managed.

InsureMyTrip is seeking a Strategic Partnerships & Communications Lead to drive growth, cultivate strategic partnerships, and elevate brand visibility through media relations, data-driven storytelling, content development, and partner engagement initiatives. This role will lead the development and execution of partnership, affiliate, and communications strategies that increase brand awareness, drive customer acquisition and revenue growth, strengthen industry relationships, and position InsureMyTrip as the trusted authority in travel insurance and travel protection. The ideal candidate is a strong relationship builder, strategic communicator, and storyteller with experience in partnerships, public relations, affiliate marketing, and content strategy. Leverage AI-powered tools to enhance content creation, research, media outreach, partnership development, reporting, and overall workflow efficiency. 40% Partnerships/Growth, 30% Communications/PR, 20% Content & Research, 10% Reporting/Administration Skills and Experience Needed: Bachelor's degree in Public Relations, Communications, Marketing, Journalism, Business, or a related field. 2+ years of experience in partnerships, public relations, affiliate marketing, content marketing, communications, or a related field. Experience supporting earned media initiatives and building relationships with media contacts. Experience recruiting, managing, or growing affiliate, referral, partner, or business development programs. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong editing, interpersonal, and relationship-building abilities. Ability to analyze data and insights to help inform marketing, communications, and partnership strategies. Working knowledge of affiliate marketing platforms, SEO best practices, content marketing, and digital analytics tools. Preferred Qualifications Experience in travel, insurance, fintech, e-commerce, or consumer services industries. Experience developing original research, consumer surveys, trend reports, rankings, or data-driven marketing campaigns. Experience working with affiliate networks, partnership platforms, or performance marketing programs. What We Offer Hybrid Schedule, 2 days work from home and 3 days in office  Strong learning culture with ongoing development opportunities Medical, vision, and dental coverage, Basic life and disability insurance 401(k) plan  If you are a motivated professional with the skills and experience to succeed in this role, we encourage you to apply and join our team. Join a team where your success is our priority and you can make a real impact! The pay range for this position is $74,600 – $93,300 which includes geographic adjustments, where applicable. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about — helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses. To further this mission, we’re looking for a marketer to join our Co-Marketing team focused on reaching the DoorDash Advertiser audience. Our Co-Marketing team partners with DoorDash's most valued Enterprise Advertisers to create integrated marketing programs that acquire new customers and drive sales and awareness for our mutual businesses. Our North Star is to be the most trusted and sought-after co-marketing partner for brands by creating groundbreaking marketing that delivers value to our mutual audiences, drives business impact for our Advertisers, and puts our brands at the center of culture. About the Role The Ads Co-Marketing team is looking for a strategic, entrepreneurial, and data-driven marketer to own and grow our co-marketing opportunities with DoorDash's leading Enterprise Restaurant partners. Reporting to the Sr. Manager, Restaurant Merchant Partnerships, you'll be the day-to-day owner for a book of Restaurant Advertisers - owning the relationship, strategy, and execution that keeps our partners engaged and growing on DoorDash. You'll work closely with Sales, Growth Marketing, and Creative Studio to ensure we're maximizing value from our partner relationships, with marketing that drives our partners' business forward and serves our shared audiences. This is a unique opportunity to help shape a fast-growing, global consumer brand through the lens of our partnerships. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Own and grow marketing relationships with some of our largest and most high-profile Enterprise Restaurant partners — serving as lead for co-marketing engagements, including annual/quarterly strategic planning, campaign execution, and alignment across internal and external stakeholders Lead the strategy and execution of integrated co-marketing campaigns end-to-end — from concept and production through launch, optimization, and reporting — bringing strong operational rigor and organization to keep complex, multi-team campaigns on track, in close partnership with Sales, Creative, Paid Media, Social, and Operations teams Apply a data-first mindset to measure, analyze, and continuously optimize campaign performance — delivering clear, actionable readouts (internal and partner-facing) tied to success measures like ads revenue growth, merchant growth, incremental order volume, and advertiser engagement and retention Bring the restaurant advertiser's point of view into broader conversations across DoorDash Marketing — helping shape new co-marketing opportunities and supporting the sales team in pitching them to partners when needed Manage campaign budgets, including spend tracking, pacing, and accrual preparation, to ensure efficient investment and strong ROI We’re excited about you because you have… 6+ years of B2C marketing at a consumer brand, tech company, media agency, or consultancy, with a mix of performance, retention, and consulting experience; MBA a plus. A proven track record of owning marketing programs end-to-end — from goal-setting and strategy through execution, optimization, and performance reporting — with hands-on experience across paid media platforms (e.g., Google, Meta, TikTok) and CRM channels in a client- or partner-facing environment; restaurant industry experience a plus. Strong analytical skills, including market and segment sizing, forecasting, and using data to inform decisions and optimize performance. Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills — including experience partnering with a sales or sales/marketing organization to drive advertiser outcomes across Marketing, Sales, Strategy & Operations, Analytics, Product, and Creative teams. A creative, entrepreneurial mindset — comfortable solving ambiguous problems and building solutions in fast-paced, resource-constrained environments. This role acts as a key partner to Sales, Product, and Strategic Accounts to translate ecosystem dynamics, customer needs, and market insights into impactful co-marketing programs and partnerships across the data center value chain.Essential Duties and Responsibilities Develop and execute strategic partnership marketing plans aligned to Gates’ Data Center growth strategy. Identify, prioritize, and manage key ecosystem partnerships including OEMs, hyperscalers, colocation providers, engineering firms, and system integrators. Design and execute co-marketing initiatives such as joint events, campaigns, technical content, and thought leadership with partners. Enable Sales and Strategic Account teams with partner-driven marketing tools, messaging, and campaigns to accelerate pipeline growth. Align ‘push’ (OEM, channel, partners) and ‘pull’ (end users, hyperscalers) marketing motions to create a cohesive go-to-market approach. Collaborate with product management and engineering to effectively position Gates’ data center assembly and fluid conveyance solutions. Own partner marketing performance metrics including lead generation, pipeline impact, and ROI of campaigns and partnerships. Manage relationships with external partners and agencies to ensure high-quality execution and consistent brand messaging. Develop compelling value propositions and messaging tailored to key data center customer segments. Analyze market trends, customer insights, and competitive activity to refine partnership marketing strategy. Requirements and Preferred Skills Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, or related field. 8+ years of experience in strategic marketing, partnership marketing, or business development roles. Experience working with partners and executing co-marketing programs in a B2B or industrial environment. Strong understanding of data center market dynamics and ecosystem players preferred. Proven ability to collaborate across sales, product, and marketing organizations. Strong communication, project management, and analytical skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience in data center infrastructure, liquid cooling, or thermal management markets. Familiarity with fluid systems, assemblies, or industrial manufacturing solutions. Experience supporting global or multi-region marketing programs. Ability to translate technical concepts into customer-facing marketing content. Strategic and commercial mindset with ability to connect partnerships to business growth. Strong relationship-building and influence skills across internal and external stakeholders. Ability to operate in a fast-paced, evolving market environment. Data-driven decision-making and performance tracking. Collaborative, proactive, and results-oriented approach. Competencies Strategic and commercial mindset with ability to connect partnerships to business growth. Strong relationship-building and influence skills across internal and external stakeholders. Ability to operate in a fast-paced, evolving market environment. Data-driven decision-making and performance tracking. Collaborative, proactive, and results-oriented approach. Pay & Benefits Full-Time Salary Range: $120,000 - $155,000 Relocation is not provided Medical, Dental, Vision insurance and other voluntary benefit options: benefits begin on the first day of the month immediately following your date of hire Eligible for 3 weeks of paid vacation + 11 holidays (9 scheduled & 2 floating) + 8 sick days. This is a hands-on coordinator role, not administrative support. • 18-20 hours per week. • $20-$26 per hour, based on experience. • Reports to Christina Marcaccini, CMO. Mission Take over day-to-day performance strategy, measurement, launch readiness, and delivery prioritization for a defined portfolio of EIC's white-label and platform clients. The goal is to move the founder from routine client-delivery decisions, diagnosis, and QA into exception review while helping Account Managers communicate clearly and Ad Managers execute the approved strategy correctly. This is a hands-on growth role, not a reporting-only or hands-off consulting position. We want someone with strong fundamentals, technical curiosity, ownership, and the humility to learn EIC's approach. The Manager must be willing to investigate abnormal performance, enter unfamiliar platforms, debug tracking and integrations, and coach the team through implementation. Responsibility and autonomy will expand as judgment and trust are demonstrated. The PodThe initial 90-day engagement is focused on one assigned pod rather than EIC's entire client roster. The Manager quarterbacks the pod through strategy, prioritization, coaching, standards, and QA. Formal direct reports are not required initially, although people-management responsibility may develop as the role expands. Account Manager: Owns client relationships, communication, timelines, and coordination.Ad Manager: Owns campaign builds, trafficking, daily optimization, testing, and routine execution.Performance Strategy & Analytics Manager: Owns business goals, channel and funnel strategy, weekly priorities, measurement, launch readiness, data quality, and final recommendations.Core ResponsibilitiesTranslate business goals into media strategy, including audience, offer, funnel, channel mix, budget, testing plan, and KPIs tied to client economics.Set the pod's weekly priorities by identifying the highest-impact risks and opportunities and turning them into a sequenced work queue for Account Managers and Ad Managers.Detect and diagnose performance problems across campaigns, creative, budgets, search terms, websites, forms, tracking, CRM, integrations, reporting, lead quality, and sales process.Direct recovery through an execution-ready plan with owners, dependencies, and acceptance criteria, then stay involved until the root cause is corrected and the result is verified in production.Own launch readiness across strategy, creative, targeting, budget, access, tracking, CRM handoff, reporting, and client approvals. Separate true blockers from work that can safely continue after launch.Own end-to-end measurement and data flow from ad platforms through websites, forms, call tracking, analytics, CRM, automation, qualified pipeline, closed-won revenue, and ROAS.Work directly inside platforms when complex setup, debugging, QA, recovery, or training requires it. Routine trafficking and daily optimization remain with the Ad Manager whenever practical.Lead client strategy conversations, quarterly recaps, media planning, and responsible forecasting using actual business performance, clear assumptions, and known constraints.Turn founder judgment into repeatable decision rules, QA standards, diagnostic processes, launch criteria, and escalation thresholds.What Success Looks LikeEvery account in the pod has an agreed business goal, funnel, KPI hierarchy, source of truth, and prioritized action plan.Material performance changes are identified early, investigated across the full system, and resolved at the root cause.Launches have verified tracking, CRM handoff, reporting, and optimization signals before avoidable problems reach the client.Account Managers know what to communicate, Ad Managers know what to execute and why, and clients understand the strategy and tradeoffs.Founder involvement moves from routine prioritization, diagnosis, and QA to defined exception review.Each quarter closes with a clear performance story and an evidence-based next-quarter plan and forecast.Required ExperienceApproximately 6–10 years across paid media strategy, account leadership, performance marketing, marketing operations, or related work. Capability and judgment matter more than a rigid year count.Deep working knowledge of Google Ads and Meta Ads, with sound judgment across channels such as LinkedIn, programmatic, geofencing, and retargeting.Hands-on experience with GA4, Google Tag Manager, pixels or server-side events, offline conversions, call tracking, and attribution.Ability to connect websites and forms with CRM, automation, and reporting systems through native integrations, APIs, or webhooks.Ability to audit campaign builds against strategy, diagnose anomalies, and turn findings into an execution-ready repair plan.Comfort with browser developer tools, tag debugging, cookie and network inspection, platform diagnostics, and CRM record tracing. Software engineering experience is not required.Experience translating complex performance into clear client narratives, quarterly plans, and responsible forecasts.Strong business acumen across conversion rates, sales capacity, CAC, LTV, payback, pipeline, revenue, and ROAS.Strong convictions loosely held, disciplined QA, clear communication, coachability, and calm ownership under pressure.How the Role GrowsFirst 30 days: Learn EIC's framework, shadow pod reviews, audit the assigned accounts, and learn the current platforms, commitments, and workflows.Days 31–60: Prepare weekly priorities, own analysis and recommendations for selected accounts, coach an Ad Manager through implementation, and lead part of a client strategy discussion.Days 61–90: Run the pod's weekly performance review, priority queue, launch and measurement QA, planning, and client strategy conversations, with the founder reviewing exceptions rather than building the answer.Long term: Expand account and team ownership as judgment, leverage, and business need are demonstrated.Compensation and StructurePaid 90-day, part-time engagement averaging approximately 15 hours per week.Starting compensation of $4,500–$5,500 per month, based on experience and demonstrated capability.Scope, responsibility, hours, and compensation will be formally reviewed at the end of the engagement.Path to a larger part-time or full-time role for someone who demonstrates the ability to independently own the pod.Hiring Proof PointsCandidates should be prepared to walk through: A system they designed that connected ad spend to qualified pipeline or revenue.A material performance decline they diagnosed, including how they proved the root cause and validated recovery.A launch they kept on track despite access, tracking, CRM, reporting, or approval blockers.A campaign build that did not match strategy and the exact rebuild direction they provided.A recommendation they changed because CRM or business data contradicted platform data.A difficult client conversation that turned complex information into a clear decision.A time they coached an executor, documented the process, and reduced future escalations.An unfamiliar platform or system they learned quickly and how they verified the solution.

Full description

You've Never Been Satisfied with "Good Enough." You didn't get into this to manage one piece of a project. You got into it to change how the world gets built. At Accenture Construct, that's the job. You'll help deliver the data centers, power grids, rail networks, factories and public infrastructure that keep communities moving — smarter, safer and more sustainably. You'll work alongside people who think big and act bold: project managers, engineers, technologists and strategists who pair real-world delivery with AI. And you won't be handed a slice of it. We take on whole programs, from early strategy through construction and handover, and we stand behind how they land. Because “good enough” builds the past. You're here to build what's next. Visit us here to learn more about ​Accenture Construct As Accenture continues to grow, you may see a variety of new career opportunities, and depending on the role and location you may be directed to apply through Accenture LLP or one of our other legal entities - Accenture Construct LLC or Accenture Construct Inc., with benefits varying by country and role, so please check with your recruiter for details. THE WORK: You'll lead day-to-day stakeholder engagement and communications programs supporting large-scale infrastructure and capital projects. You'll serve as a trusted advisor to public agency clients, project teams, and contractors, providing strategic communications and stakeholder engagement guidance. You'll develop and implement outreach strategies that foster understanding, address concerns, and maintain positive relationships with communities, businesses, elected officials, and other key stakeholders. You'll prepare clear, compelling communications materials and executive-level messaging that translate complex technical information into accessible, audience-focused content. You'll manage public meetings, community events, stakeholder inquiries, and issue resolution efforts to support project objectives and stakeholder satisfaction. You'll analyze stakeholder feedback and provide strategic recommendations to clients and project leadership to inform decision-making and project delivery. You'll confidently present project updates, engagement strategies, and recommendations to executive leadership, elected officials, governing boards, and public audiences. You'll develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) and prepare progress reports to measure program effectiveness and communicate results to clients. You'll identify stakeholder, reputational, and political risks and support the development of proactive mitigation strategies. You'll build and maintain relationships with public agencies, contractors, teaming partners, and industry organizations throughout California. You'll identify and support the pursuit of new business opportunities across transportation, transit, water, energy, and public infrastructure markets. You'll lead and contribute to proposal development, qualifications packages, interview presentations, and grant applications. You'll develop persuasive technical narratives, executive summaries, and win themes that strengthen pursuit strategies and proposal submissions. You'll contribute to capture planning, market research, and account development activities that support business growth objectives. You'll represent Accenture at industry events, conferences, and client meetings to strengthen market presence, expand relationships, and generate new opportunities. $120,000 - $135,000 a year

This role is remote eligible in the continental U.S. with occasional business travel. Improve the handoff process between marketing and sales through clearly defined processes and KPIs. Stakeholder ManagementBuild trust with and influence senior stakeholders across business units, Marketing leadership, and Sales/Commercial organizations. Team LeadershipLead and motivate a team of marketing managers and specialists to develop and activate campaigns. Provide coaching, mentorship, and professional development. Foster a highly engaged team environment and support strong employee engagement outcomes. Marketing Team CollaborationPartner with Field Marketing to develop and support local go-to-market strategies and tactics. Collaborate with Product Marketing and Centers of Excellence (COEs) to inform value proposition development, content needs, marketing asset requirements, event planning, and subject matter expert engagement. Budget ManagementDevelop annual budget plans aligned with business priorities and maintain accurate tracking of actual spend versus forecast. Class A Misdemeanor Conviction, Deferred Adjudication or Felony Conviction are permanent disqualifiers.All applicants must pass department required testing, oral interview board, and drug/physical screening.Must pass a Federal/National criminal background investigation and credit check, psychological screening, and polygraph exam.Must have a valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record as defined by City policy and the ability to obtain a Texas driver's license in accordance with Texas State law.Must pass a pre-employment physical, drug screen, Titmus vision screening, Ishihara vision screening, and audio (whisper test) screening.Working Conditions: While performing the essential functions of this position the employee is rarely exposed to disagreeable environmental factors. Works flexible hours to include all shifts; nights, weekends, and holidays and accept on-call duty status. This position requires occasionally lifting and/or moving up to 25 pounds. This job requires the ability to work in an office environment where the noise level is usually moderate.

At Caris, we understand that cancer is an ugly word—a word no one wants to hear, but one that connects us all. That’s why we’re not just transforming cancer care—we’re changing lives. We introduced precision medicine to the world and built an industry around the idea that every patient deserves answers as unique as their DNA. Backed by cutting-edge molecular science and AI, we ask ourselves every day: “What would I do if this patient were my mom?” That question drives everything we do. But our mission doesn’t stop with cancer. We're pushing the frontiers of medicine and leading a revolution in healthcare—driven by innovation, compassion, and purpose. Join us in our mission to improve the human condition across multiple diseases. If you're passionate about meaningful work and want to be part of something bigger than yourself, Caris is where your impact begins. Position Summary The Marketing Manager supports the execution of commercial marketing initiatives and user experience programs for Caris’ oncology diagnostics portfolio. This position coordinates the development, review, production, distribution, and maintenance of customer-facing marketing materials and laboratory support collateral. The Marketing Manager also helps capture, organize, and communicate customer feedback to support continuous improvement initiatives. Working under the direction of the Senior Director, this individual partners with Marketing, Product Management, Laboratory Operations, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Commercial, Supply Chain, and external creative partners to ensure materials are accurate, compliant, visually consistent, and delivered on time. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, collaborative, and passionate about creating an exceptional customer experience through effective coordination, communication, and execution. Job Responsibilities Coordinate the development, review, approval, production, distribution, and maintenance of customer-facing marketing materials. Manage timelines and deliverables for commercial collateral, ensuring projects progress efficiently through review, approval, and production. Partner with internal stakeholders and external creative agencies to develop high-quality marketing materials that align with brand standards and business objectives. Maintain version control and organization of marketing assets to ensure teams have access to current, approved materials. Coordinate the development and maintenance of laboratory support materials, including: Test Request Forms, Specimen requirement guides, Collection instructions, Kit inserts, Provider reference materials, Patient-facing educational materials, Laboratory collateral Work closely with graphic designers to translate technical and clinical content into clear, user-friendly materials. Coordinate updates to collection kits, printed components, packaging materials, labels, and specification sheets. Partner with Laboratory Operations, Product Management, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, Supply Chain, and external vendors to ensure materials remain accurate, compliant, and current. Support user experience initiatives by coordinating the collection, organization, and documentation of feedback from healthcare providers, laboratory partners, patients, and commercial teams. Develop and maintain standardized processes for collecting, categorizing, and tracking customer feedback across multiple channels. Organize and analyze customer insights to identify trends, recurring pain points, and opportunities to improve the customer experience. Support the prioritization of user experience enhancements by maintaining feedback logs, dashboards, and reporting tools. Coordinate cross-functional review sessions to communicate customer insights and track progress on improvement initiatives. Coordinate meetings, project timelines, and follow-up activities across multiple departments. Track deliverables, approvals, and action items to ensure projects remain organized and on schedule. Facilitate communication among Marketing, Laboratory Operations, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Commercial, Product Management, and external partners. Identify potential risks or delays and communicate them proactively to the Senior Director. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Life Sciences, or a related field. Three to five years of experience in marketing, marketing coordination, healthcare communications, or a related role. Strong organizational and project coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Experience coordinating creative projects with internal stakeholders and external design partners. Exceptional attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to producing high-quality deliverables. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, specifically Word, Excel, and Outlook, with a general working knowledge of the Internet for business use. Preferred Qualifications Experience in oncology, diagnostics, biotechnology, healthcare, or life sciences. Familiarity with laboratory workflows, diagnostic testing, or regulated healthcare marketing. Experience supporting Voice of Customer, customer experience, or user experience initiatives. Experience using project management and collaboration platforms such as Smartsheet, Asana, or similar tools. Training All job-specific, safety, and compliance training is assigned based on the job functions associated with this employee. Posting Date 10/12/2026225 E Germann RdSte 150, Gilbert, Arizona, 85297-2909, United States of America We are seeking a mission-driven Partner Marketing Administrator to build awareness of health plans that offer the support of DaVita’s value-based care program through direct, local engagement with kidney care patients. You will spend time in dialysis clinics, engage with eligible patients and caregivers, and build trust that leads to informed health insurance decisions. You’ll also work closely with care teams and local leadership to understand how the care management program works alongside strong health plan benefits to support this patient community. Note: You must possess or be willing to obtain the required licensure to educate on health plans in the state of Arizona, called the Life and Health Insurance License . If you are selected for the role but do not possess the required licensure, DaVita will reimburse the cost of obtaining the licensure. At Prologis, we don’t just lead the industry—we define it with a 1.3 billion square foot portfolio and an annual throughput of approximately $3.2 trillion. We create the intelligent infrastructure that powers global commerce, seamlessly connecting the digital and physical worlds. Job Title Director, Marketing – Digital Customer Experience Company Prologis A day in the life The Director, Marketing – Digital Customer Experience will lead the strategy and evolution of Prologis’ global digital customer experience ecosystem with an AI-first transformation mindset. This role sits at the intersection of Marketing, Customer Experience, Technology, Data, and AI, translating business priorities into scalable digital capabilities that improve how customers, prospects, marketers, and internal teams engage with Prologis. The Director will own the vision and roadmap across digital experience platforms, including web and CMS, property search, digital asset management, marketing automation, analytics, personalization, conversational experiences, and AI-enabled capabilities. A core expectation of this role is to continually reimagine Digital Customer Experience through AI, automation, and data. The Director will challenge existing customer journeys, content operations, marketing workflows, search experiences, personalization, analytics, and team processes to determine where AI can simplify, automate, augment, or fundamentally redesign the way work gets done and experiences are delivered. AI should be considered from the outset when defining new digital capabilities rather than added after solutions have been designed. This leader will translate Prologis’ broader enterprise AI strategy into actionable Digital Customer Experience priorities and use cases, while partnering closely with Enterprise AI, Technology, Architecture, Data, Security, Privacy, Legal, and governance teams on shared platforms, standards, and responsible AI practices. The Internal Communications Lead will serve as a communications partner to Global Strategic Marketing (GSM) leadership, translating business priorities, transformation initiatives, and key updates into clear, consistent communications for the organization. This person combines strong judgment and exceptional writing with the ability to connect activity across multiple initiatives, bring structure to ambiguity, and turn broad direction into clear, finished communications. Part-time contract role: up to 20 hrs/ week Location Remote Duration 6 months (possible extension to 12 months) Compensation Starting at $80/hr W2 Responsibilities Leadership Partnership & Communications Counsel: Participate in relevant GSM leadership discussions and maintain visibility across major priorities and initiatives. Proactively identify communications needs and recommend the appropriate audience, message, channel, and timing. Communications Planning & GSM Narrative: Operationalize GSM’s internal communications approach and maintain a clear, consistent narrative connecting leadership priorities, transformation initiatives, milestones, business outcomes, and key wins. Maintain an integrated communications calendar and recommend communications based on emerging needs across GSM. Transformation & Initiative Communications: Partner with Change Management and initiative leaders to translate change plans into clear, coordinated communications. Develop messages, stakeholder communications, leader materials, FAQs, and communications cadences that support awareness, understanding, and adoption. Leadership Messaging & Talking Points: Develop executive communications, presentations, leadership updates, briefing materials, and reusable talking points that equip leaders and GSM team members to explain priorities and initiatives consistently. Content Development, Storytelling & Wins: Translate complex topics into clear, practical, and engaging communications for diverse audiences. Develop emails, Teams messages, presentations, FAQs, newsletters, leader materials, and stories that make GSM priorities, progress, and key wins visible and understandable. Town Halls & Employee Engagement: Support the planning and execution of town halls and employee engagement activities, including messaging, creative concepts, presentation development, speaker preparation, and follow-up communications. Communications Operations & Channels: Establish and maintain the working structure for GSM communications, including planning routines, intake and prioritization, editorial cadence, calendars, templates, content repositories, and channel delivery across Staffbase, Teams, SharePoint, email, and other employee communications platforms. Measurement & Insights: Monitor communications performance and employee feedback, using engagement data and insights to improve effectiveness and inform future communications. Requirements 7+ years of relevant internal, corporate, or transformation communications experience, or equivalent experience demonstrating the ability to independently counsel leaders and execute communications in a complex organization. Demonstrated ability to work independently from broad or incomplete direction. Strong judgment about what needs to be communicated, to whom, when, and through which channel. Ability to stay informed across multiple initiatives without needing to be the subject-matter expert for each. Comfort participating in leadership discussions and handling confidential or evolving information. Ability to connect disparate updates into a consistent organizational narrative. Strong writing, editing, storytelling, and executive communications capabilities. Experience supporting transformation, organizational change, or major business initiatives through communications. Skilled at developing communications plans, leadership messaging, town halls, employee engagement activities, and channel content. Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and follow through. Data-informed mindset and experience using communications metrics and feedback to improve effectiveness. Equally comfortable advising leaders and producing the finished deliverables. Highly proactive, low-ego, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities and information may evolve quickly. Please apply today!

Job Description Job Description Peak Energy Job Title: Senior Manager, Communications Location: Burlingame, California (In-person) Department: Marketing Reports To: Director of Growth & Marketing Position Type: Full-time About Peak Energy Peak Energy is the first American venture to advance globally proven Sodium-Ion battery systems as the storage standard for the new era of renewable energy on a resilient grid. Sodium-Ion is cheap, readily available and safe, making it the leading contender in a rapidly evolving market. Our leadership team is powered by decades of expertise in scaling gigawatt-level innovation at world-class companies such as Tesla, Northvolt, Apple, Powin, Enovix, Zipline, Solid Power, and Fluence. We are backed by strategic investment and product partners such as TDK Ventures and Eclipse Ventures. We are a team of engineers, operators, entrepreneurs, and partners driven by a shared ambition to set the new performance standard for renewable energy and grid resilience. About the Role – Senior Manager, Communications Peak Energy is looking for a Senior Manager, Communications to lead corporate communications, public relations, and product storytelling. You will work closely with Peak's leadership team and across Marketing, Commercial, Product, and Engineering to shape how we communicate our company, technology, and products externally. You'll turn company priorities, customer insights, and complex technical inputs into clear, compelling narratives. This is a hands-on role that spans strategy and execution. You will write press releases, develop messaging and media pitches, prepare executives for interviews, shape product positioning, and lead major announcements from initial strategy through launch. What You'll Do (Responsibilities) Corporate Communications & Executive Communications Develop and execute Peak's corporate communications and PR strategy. Work directly with executives to develop messaging, talking points, presentations, and external narratives. Write press releases, media pitches, FAQs, briefing materials, and executive communications. Prepare executives for media interviews, speaking engagements, and major announcements. Build media relationships and proactively drive earned coverage. Manage Peak's external PR agency, including priorities, pitching strategy, and performance. Positioning, Content & Storytelling Develop and maintain Peak's corporate, technology, and product messaging. Translate technical differentiation, customer insights, and market dynamics into clear value propositions and compelling external stories. Partner with Commercial, Product, and Engineering to validate proof points, customer evidence, and technical claims. Develop executive thought leadership and review technical explainers, case studies, white papers, and customer-facing content to ensure messaging alignment Partner with executives and subject matter experts to develop differentiated points of view on key market topics. Launches & Go-to-Market Communications Lead communications for product launches, customer announcements, partnerships, financing, manufacturing milestones, and other major company news. Partner with Government Affairs, Product, Commercial, and Engineering to translate GTM strategy into positioning, proof points, launch narratives, and supporting materials. Own communications execution from narrative and content development through media strategy and external rollout. What You'll Bring (Qualifications) 6–8+ years of experience in communications, PR, product communications, or a related role. Exceptional writer and editor with extensive experience writing press releases, pitches, executive messaging, and long-form content. Strong media relations experience and a track record of securing meaningful earned coverage. Experience working directly with senior executives and the judgment and confidence to advise leadership on messaging and external communications. Experience positioning and launching technical products, technologies, or major company initiatives. Ability to translate complex technical and commercial information into clear, credible narratives and customer value propositions. High ownership and ability to move between strategy and hands-on execution. Preferred Qualifications Significant PR agency experience strongly preferred, ideally combined with in-house experience. Experience in energy, infrastructure, climate tech, industrial technology, or another technical industry strongly preferred. Peak Energy is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. We strongly encourage women, people of color, and individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. We value skills, potential, and perspective over specific credentials. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't look perfect on paper, we still want to hear from you. Our Core Values Speed Through Focus - Move fast but understand why. Focus on the goal, don't sacrifice quality. Mission Over Self - It's about the greater good; confident humility. Take ownership and accountability. Face the Brutal Truth - Transparency, honesty, big picture curiosity. Fearless decision making. Be a Good Person - Kindness, collaboration and teamwork. Compensation & Benefits The salary range for this role is $120,000-$200,000 , with actual pay varying based on work location, experience, and skills. Our competitive benefits package includes: Flexible time off Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage Strong 401(k) plan Equity opportunities Many great work perks Join us to thrive in a supportive environment while making a meaningful impact in the energy sector! At Peak Energy Technologies Inc., we believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace makes us a more capable, innovative, and competitive company. We welcome people who represent diversity in their backgrounds, ethnicities, cultures, and experiences. Peak Energy Technologies Inc. is an equal opportunity employer, aiming to reach our company's full potential by cultivating an inclusive workforce. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

Position Overview Arizona Sports Enterprises (ASE), the sponsorship and NIL arm of Arizona Athletics, is seeking a Director Partnership Marketing to lead the strategy, execution, and fulfillment of all corporate partnerships. In this Full-Time, Exempt role based in Tucson, AZ, you will ensure best-in-class partner activation, retention, and service delivery across Arizona Athletics. You will also manage and develop the Partnership Marketing team, oversee the sponsorship lifecycle, and serve as a strategic partner to sales, campus stakeholders, and senior leadership. The ideal candidate demonstrates leadership, operational rigor, and creative problem-solving with the ability to scale processes while preserving a high-touch partner experience. Key Responsibilities Leadership & Team Management: Lead, coach, and develop the Partnership Marketing team to ensure consistent, high-quality partner service. Conduct regular one-on-one meetings, performance feedback, and professional development planning. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Serve as a resource to troubleshoot and resolve activation challenges in real time. Partnership Marketing & Activation: Own the activation and fulfillment strategy for all corporate partnerships across Arizona Athletics. Manage the full sponsorship lifecycle, including onboarding, execution, measurement, and renewal support. Ensure all contractual elements are delivered accurately, on time, and in alignment with brand standards. Build and maintain strong relationships with corporate partners to support renewals and long-term growth. Develop scalable activation frameworks, timelines, and recap materials for internal and external use. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with internal Athletics and campus stakeholders (Ticketing, Marketing, Communications, Game Operations, Community Impact, NIL, Legal, Procurement, Licensing, Digital, Media Relations, and Compliance) to streamline approvals and ensure execution accuracy. Operational Excellence: Develop and manage a comprehensive activation calendar across all partners and sports. Oversee onboarding and training of new Partnership Marketing staff. Continuously evaluate and improve internal processes to enhance efficiency and partner satisfaction. Support the development of partner recaps, case studies, and performance reporting. Partner with analytics resources to evaluate brand exposure, engagement, and return on objectives. Sales & Revenue Integration: Collaborate with the sales team to review partnership structures for feasibility and accuracy. Provide activation input during the sales process as needed. Support renewal strategy and identification of growth opportunities within existing accounts. Maintain working knowledge of partner categories, exclusivities, inventory, and asset availability. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required. Minimum of 5 years of experience in partnership marketing, sponsorship activation, or account management. Minimum of 2 years of people management experience. Experience working in sports, entertainment, higher education, or a related partnership-driven environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience in pro sports, collegiate athletics, or multi-property sponsorship environments. Demonstrated success leading cross-functional teams. Experience working with CRM systems and sponsorship analytics tools.
